title: OmniPortrait: Fine-Grained Personalized Portrait Synthesis via Pivotal Optimization
claim: Existing methods lose fine-grained facial detail; ours preserves identity and prompt alignment, and extends to multiple identities.
layout: 2 stacked panels; (a) side-by-side comparison with zoom-in insets, (b) reference-to-output grid
description: The figure has two stacked panels. Panel (a), 'Comparison on Facial Detail Generation', starts with an ID reference portrait of a smiling woman. Next to it are three generated results for the prompt 'a woman wearing headphones with auburn hair in a living room': Instant-ID and PhotoMaker in gray dashed boxes, and 'Ours' in a red dashed box. Each result has a red-boxed face region linked by lines to a magnified inset, which shows how well the facial details are kept. Panel (b), 'Identity-Consistent Portrait Generation', has two reference faces, a woman and a man, on the left. Beside them are prompts with the gendered words highlighted in orange, such as riding a horse near a castle and spraying graffiti. Next to the prompts are 'Ours (single)' outputs for each identity. At the right are 'Ours (multiple)' images of the two people together by a lake and at dinner. The red 'Ours' highlight draws the eye first.
caption: We demonstrate (a) the challenges faced by existing methods in customizing fine-grained facial features, and (b) that OmniPortrait is able to generate images with exceptional identity similarity, strong text–image alignment and can be extended to multi-identity customization.
abstract: Image identity customization aims to synthesize realistic and diverse portraits of a specified identity, given a reference image and a text prompt. This task presents two key challenges: (1) generating realistic portraits that preserve fine-grained facial details of the reference identity, and (2) maintaining identity consistency while achieving strong alignment with the text prompt. Our findings suggest that existing single-stream methods fail to capture and guide fine-grained identity details. To address these challenges, we introduce \textit{OmniPortrait}, a novel diffusion-based framework for fine-grained identity fidelity and high editability in portrait synthesis. Our core idea is pivotal optimization, which leverages dual-stream identity guidance in a coarse-to-fine manner. First, a Pivot ID Encoder is proposed and trained with a face localization loss while avoiding the degradation of editability typically caused by fine-tuning the denoiser. Although this encoder primarily guides coarse-level identity synthesis, it provides a good initialization that serves as the identity pivot for optimization during inference. Second, we propose Reference-Based Guidance, which performs on-the-fly feature matching and optimization over diffusion intermediate features conditioned on the identity pivot. In addition, our approach is able to generalize naturally to multi-identity customized image generation scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements in both identity preservation and text alignment, establishing a new benchmark for image identity customization.
